changes.after: Two objects can work with the same method if each responds to the operation that method needs.

before: show asks its argument for label. The two classes need no shared custom parent or declared interface for this call to work: this is duck typing.

Having a method name is not enough to guarantee its argument rules, return meaning or side effects. The caller and implementations still need a clear behavior contract and tests. Missing methods are reported when the call executes.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
class Card
  def label
    "card"
  end
end
class Bookmark
  def label
    "bookmark"
  end
end
def show(item)
  puts item.label
end
show(Card.new)
show(Bookmark.new)
```

Expected output or behavior: card
bookmark. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

The code does not need both objects to belong to the same class.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby

  end
end
def show(item)
  puts item.label
end
show(Card.new)
show(Bookmark.new)
```
The output is `card`, then `bookmark`. Card and Bookmark each have a label method.
